capabilities.wealth_summary: ADCB runs a Private Banking and Wealth Management business reported as the Private Banking segment (FY2025 operating income AED 1.84bn, 8% of group; H1 2026 AED 0.72bn, 6%). It does not publish AUM, but says 'assets under management within investment and advisory solutions' grew 50% in 2025 and 27% yoy to Jun 2026, with the private-banking client base up 26% yoy and 277 new clients in Q4 2025. Its stated aim is to be 'the private bank of choice in the region' through holistic advisory, discretionary portfolio management, wealth planning and integrated financing on a 'sophisticated investment platform' (Q1 2026). Retail Banking reports healthy investment and insurance flows and launched 'new digital investment capabilities' in 2025, then a new AI-enabled mobile app with a conversational AI interface in Q2 2026; product details were not accessible. Net 'asset mgt./investment services' fees were AED 267m in FY2025 (+23%) and AED 148m in H1 2026 (+18%). Al Hilal Bank is a fully digital Islamic retail bank; no Islamic wealth products were evidenced. Product pages (Excellency, ADCB Securities, private banking) could not be checked because adcb.com and alhilalbank.ae returned HTTP 403.

Group-wide AI-led transformation programme targeting AED 4bn of financial value; 150+ use cases, dedicated AI leadership and 'partnerships with global AI leaders' (unnamed); internal tools Enterprise Knowledge, Board Observer, Credit Companion

opportunities: Fast-growing private bank: AUM within investment and advisory solutions +50% yoy in 2025 and +27% yoy at Jun 2026; client base +26% yoy (S1, S3).
Stated ambition to be 'the private bank of choice in the region' through advisory, discretionary management and wealth planning on a 'sophisticated investment platform' (S5).
Retail is adding digital investing: 'new digital investment capabilities' (2025) and a new AI-enabled app with a conversational AI interface (Q2 2026); specifics not published (S1, S3).
Group AI programme targets AED 4bn of value across 150+ use cases; named AI tools so far are internal (knowledge, credit, board), none for wealth clients or RMs (S3, S4).
Investment fee line is small: net 'asset mgt./investment services' fees AED 267m in FY2025 vs net fees AED 3,607m (S4).
Al Hilal Bank has a fully digital Islamic retail base (>95% of active customers digital) but no Islamic investment product evidenced (S3).
barriers: In-house AI transformation with dedicated AI leadership, specialist delivery teams and unnamed 'global AI leaders' as partners (S3).
Meedaf is ADCB's own vehicle for fintech partnerships and investments (Brink's JV, InDebted) (S3).
Capital and management attention focused on corporate lending growth and a 2030 profit target; Private Banking is 6–8% of operating income (S2, S4).
